key_insight: AI agents could deepen societal inequality when people have unequal access to them or differ in the quality and number of agents they can use. The paper offers a conceptual framework for understanding these risks and a research agenda for addressing them.
problem_solved: Provides a structured way to examine how unequal access to AI agents—and differences in their capabilities and availability—could create or reinforce inequality.
method: Develop a conceptual framework to identify potential sources of inequality involving AI agents.
Examine disparities in access, agent quality, and the number of agents available to different users.
Propose a research agenda to better understand and address the resulting societal challenges.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper highlights why agent access and distribution matter alongside technical performance. It encourages attention to who benefits from agentic systems and who risks being left behind.
visual_elements: Three-axis diagram showing access, agent quality, and agent quantity as dimensions of inequality.
Side-by-side illustrations of users with different levels of agent support.
Conceptual flowchart linking unequal agent resources to potential societal disparities.
Research roadmap connecting sources of inequality to questions for future investigation.
paper_authors: Matthew Sharp, Omer Bilgin, Iason Gabriel, Lewis Hammond
